Automated decision making system to determine the risk represented by visa applicants

In August 2020, the UK government's Home Office abandoned an ADM system called the "Streaming tool"" that assessed the risk of visa applicants. The algorithm faced legal challenges from the Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants (JCWI) and Foxglove
as it was believed to perpetuate racism and bias in the visa system. The algorithm suffered from ""feedback loop"" issues

where past bias and discrimination influenced future outcomes. It prioritized applicants from predominantly white countries and subjected people from other nations to a more rigorous review process. In response to the criticism
the Home Office announced plans to redesign the ADM system
explicitly addressing concerns about unconscious bias and the use of nationality in the new system."
an AI-based speech-to-text tool in various languages"

Luxembourgish is central to the country’s linguistic identity, but speech-recognition technologies often perform better for larger languages with more abundant training data. “Sproocherkennung fir d’Lëtzebuergescht” addresses this gap by improving the speech-to-text capabilities of schreifmaschinn.lu, an AI-based transcription tool developed by the Zenter fir d’Lëtzebuerger Sprooch. The operational problem is that accurate speech recognition requires high-quality synchronised audio and text data, representing different speakers, accents, contexts and recording situations. The existing dataset already provides a foundation for Luxembourgish transcription, but broader and more diverse training material is needed to improve recognition quality and spelling accuracy. The initiative expands the hypersynchronised audio-text dataset from 55 hours to 80 hours, with two main objectives: diversifying the range of speakers and situations represented in the data, and improving orthographic accuracy in the generated transcription. At operational level, the project strengthens the data foundation behind Luxembourgish speech technology, enabling better automatic transcription for public, educational, cultural and administrative uses. It also supports digital inclusion by making spoken Luxembourgish more usable in digital environments, from accessibility tools to language-learning resources and public-service interfaces. The expected impact is more accurate Luxembourgish speech-to-text, stronger support for multilingual digital services and greater visibility of Luxembourgish in AI-enabled communication systems. The initiative is relevant because it treats language resources as strategic digital infrastructure for public-sector innovation and linguistic diversity.
Zenter fir d'Lëtzebuerger Sprooch (ZLS – Centre for Luxembourgish Language)
Empowering Local Government: A Sovereign and Human-Centric AI Strategy for Inclusive Citizen Services and Administrative Efficiency
The City of Hamm drives a holistic "People
Technology"" transformation via a structured four-pillar AI architecture: (1) ""Tom Hamme""
a 24/7 citizen chatbot supporting 100+ native languages including Easy Language for inclusive public services; (2) ""IDA""
self-hosted internal AI assistant for text-heavy tasks; (3) AI-enhanced RPA for end-to-end process automation; and (4) AI-powered specialized municipal software.
By hosting core internal AI operations locally
the city avoids vendor lock-in and ensures strict data sovereignty aligned with EU values. Our key differentiator is a human-centric approach to change management. Moving beyond mere IT deployment
a city-wide e-learning program proactively fulfills the AI literacy mandate of the EU AI Act (Art. 4). Complemented by an internal ""AI Lab"" for iterative
this strategy ensures a compliant and resilient digital transformation for civil servants and citizens alike.

VERA (Air Quality Digital Twin of the Emilia-Romagna Region)

VERA (Air Quality Digital Twin of the Emilia-Romagna Region) is a cutting-edge environmental governance digital twin platform designed to simulate, predict, and visualize territorial and environmental responses to public policies. Funded with â‚¬3M via PR FESR 2021-2027, VERA acts as a decision-support system accelerating the region's path toward air quality improvement and carbon neutrality. By integrating complex multi-source data (IoT, real-time traffic data, environmental data and Copernicus satellite feeds), VERA enables public administrators to model emissions and concentrations of key pollutants (PM10, PM2.5, NOx) through dynamic "what-if"" scenarios. Structurally aligned with Europe's Digital Valley goals
the platform features specialized environments: VERA for simulations by regional public authorities
VERA City for 3D high-resolution (50x50m grid) micro-territorial zoom monitoring and impact of local actions
and VERA People for open citizen engagement."
Marche Region’s AI Use Cases related to public procurement, implemented within the projects: “#REG4IA - AI Hubs for PAs”, “ERDF 1.2.2.1 Advanced AI Solutions for public services”, “TrasparenzAI”

Marche Region uses AI to streamline administrative procedures through three converging public-procurement initiatives.  
Under the nationally funded interregional project #Reg4IA, Marche runs a PoC using generative and ontology-based AI to assist contracting officers with tender-idcode requests, compliance checklists, drafting of contracts and payment decrees, and timeline planning, under strict human-in-the-loop oversight.  
This builds on Marche's own AI platform (AIMA, ERDF 2021-27, measure 1.2.2.1), offering customised agent-automation tools and innovative features - including contextual know-how enrichment - reusable in multi-tenant mode by other PAs.  
Lastly, under an ANAC-CNR protocol and an agreement now being signed with ANAC, the "TrasparenzAI"" project will test AI web-scraping to verify public-contract data PAs must publish in the ""Transparent Administration"" and ""Public Customer's Profile"" website sections
standardising data collection and strengthening transparency nationwide."
